doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Growing up in Brooklyn and starting piano
summary: Born in Flatbush, raised in Bensonhurst; piano lessons from age ten.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Right. Let me take you back if we can. You grew up in Brooklyn?
Did you grow up in New York?
Oh yeah. I was born in Brooklyn, born in Bensonhurst and raised in — sorry — I was born in Flatbush and raised in the Bensonhurst area. Bay Ridge, Bensonhurst.
Can you recall the first kinds of music that entered your—

Yeah, it was my first studies. When I was ten years old we had a piano in the house, and the girl next door was taking piano lessons and Mom didn’t want to be left out. She said why don’t you take some piano lessons, which I didn’t really want to do. But once I got into it I found it came easy. I kept skipping ahead to the next lesson. And before you
knew it the teacher was giving me extra stuff and I bypassed this girl and that guy and everything. It came pretty easy and the mechanics of it was — I found it quite interesting.
